title: Predictive Maintenance & Asset Performance
breadcrumb: Solutions > Operational Excellence > Predictive Maintenance & Asset Performance
meta_description: Predictive Maintenance & Asset Performance — composed architecture, platform stack and the metric the program answers to.

blocks.x: Predictive Maintenance & Asset Performance delivered as an operating capability for the enterprise, not a slide deck — durable runtime, policy-checked actions, and telemetry your auditors can read without translation.
The problem this solution exists for
Assets run to failure on calendar PMs; telemetry exists but doesn't reach planning; predictions that aren't trusted get ignored.
Our approach

We instrument the failure modes that pay, build physics-informed RUL models validated on work-order history, wire predictions into EAM/CMMS scheduling with parts staging, and manage false-alarm discipline as a first-class metric.
Reference architecture

blocks.title: Governed lakehouse pipeline — Predictive Maintenance & Asset Performance
blocks.note: Contracts between stages are enforced at the boundary, so schema drift fails loudly in minutes instead of quietly in a quarter.

blocks.x: The architecture for Predictive Maintenance & Asset Performance is deliberately auditable: every stage exposes its inputs, its owner and its failure policy, and the decision path shares a timeline with the audit path. Nothing important happens off the record.

blocks.x: Platform stack

The solution runs on BI & Analytics Platform and EEMS Platform: Sensor data feeds a living model of your plant, fleet or field estate, and the model drives action. Enterprise decisions in milliseconds — with a full evidence trail for each decision.

Quarterly re-audits and a ranked backlog of the next decisions worth automating — value that accumulates on purpose.

blocks.x: Prerequisites and data readiness

The readiness work for Predictive Maintenance & Asset Performance is unglamorous and decisive — data contracts, access paths and owner names. Programs that skip it discover the gaps at the first gate, which is the most expensive place to find them.
How a delivery runs

Delivery on Predictive Maintenance & Asset Performance is sequenced so the measurement always precedes the build: two weeks of baseline before the pilot, a scheduled gate before any scale-out, and a fortnightly reading against the signed number.
Outcomes we commit to

items: The commitment on unplanned downtime is written into the engagement charter — scope, owner and the measurement method agreed before delivery begins.
maintenance cost/unit is part of the steering pack from week two: current value, signed baseline and the delta since the last gate, on one line.
planner trust is tracked weekly to your control owner; the number at gate three is the number finance sees
